claim: The summary omits that committed refs/heads/main is authoritative and the visible checkout can differ from the graph state the daemon reads.
evidence: The document says 'Graph state lives in a dedicated Git repository' and lists 'The Git-tracked state', mentioning only 'checkout status' locally. src/store/git.rs:110-128 resolves head from refs/heads/main and reads record bytes from that commit's tree, never the working tree. Real consumers use that head: src/transcripts/mod.rs:172-176 builds its CommitView from store.head(); src/transcripts/capture.rs:408-409 loads clone/session state through it. The writer likewise starts mutation from store.head() and Overlay::new at src/writer/mod.rs:277-298, then projects the committed tree to disk at src/writer/mod.rs:400-418. src/writer/worktree.rs:110-121 deliberately leaves differing disk files untouched, records dirty paths at :196-220, and writes view_rev at :221. Thus a listed seat.toml can visibly contain user edits while the daemon still uses its committed contents. This is a material ownership/persistence distinction, rather than an omitted field or layout detail.

claim: The description of .graph-local omits durable session-report ingress and preserved user files, beyond the journal and checkout-status metadata.
evidence: The document describes local state as 'SQLite journal—queued operations, reconciliation effects, retries and notices—along with saved plans, observation baselines, thread intents, daemon locks/socket/logs and checkout status' and specifically calls the journal durable recovery state. When session.report IPC fails, the real CLI producer serializes caller/session args via spool_report at src/cli/session.rs:61-78. src/transcripts/capture.rs:28-62 syncs these reports into .graph-local/session-spool/<ulid>.json; the daemon registers its consumer at src/transcripts/mod.rs:507-509. Ingestion reads them and only then admits occupancy operations at src/transcripts/capture.rs:197-205,254-280, retaining files on transient failure at :302-308 and quarantining rejected input under session-spool/rejected at :455-462. These can therefore be the only durable session identity/transcript-path evidence before journal admission. Separately, the actual post-commit checkout projection (src/writer/mod.rs:409-418) moves remaining user-edited/untracked files out of disappeared tracked directories into .graph-local/orphans/<op-or-recovery>/<old-path>, using rename at src/writer/worktree.rs:138-169. Those files contain preserved user bytes, not merely checkout status. The layout is explicitly rough and the local list says 'includes', so individual filename omissions alone would not justify a finding; the gap is the missing persistence/ownership categories and resulting incomplete picture of what local data may be irreplaceable.

claim: Processing requests store a fixed input range.
evidence: The table says "Fixed input range". Requests do persist an explicit ByteRange (src/model/request.rs:12), but the range is not fixed for the lifetime of a request. The real producer Transcripts::create_request_for_range reads the transcript and commits bookkeeping.request_create with an explicit range (src/transcripts/mod.rs:286-307). RequestCreate::apply selects overlapping pending requests (src/transcripts/mutations.rs:375-379), preserves the oldest request ID, expands keeper.range to the union, and writes that same requests/<id>.toml again (src/transcripts/mutations.rs:387-404). Thus a pending request for [0,100) can become [0,200) when a later explicit [50,200) request is created; merged peers become unresolved. The delivery consumer subsequently reads the updated rq.range (src/transcripts/delivery.rs:83-103). The range is fixed after delivery because merge candidates are restricted to Pending, so the high-level claim could be made accurate by qualifying that lifecycle boundary.

claim: The local operational state in `.graph-local/` includes daemon locks/socket/logs.
evidence: GRAPH_STATE.md:47 places the daemon socket in `.graph-local/`. src/config.rs:177 assigns InstancePaths.socket through socket_path(root), whose implementation at src/config.rs:190-199 returns `<root>/.graph-local/daemon.sock` only when that full path is shorter than 100 bytes; otherwise it returns `/private/tmp/herdr-graph-<uid>/<hash16>.sock`. This is production behavior, not merely a schema/test possibility: src/daemon/mod.rs:46-54 creates the socket's parent directory, explicitly handles a parent outside the instance root, and src/daemon/mod.rs:102 binds the resulting path; src/daemon/client.rs:127-128 computes the same fallback and connects to it. The summary is deliberately rough, so this is a narrow location exception rather than a broader ownership mismatch, but the unqualified directory claim is false for long instance paths and may mislead someone locating a running daemon's socket.

claim: The summary does not identify refs/heads/main as authoritative or explain that the listed files are a derived checkout which can differ from effective graph state.
evidence: The document says "Graph state lives in a dedicated Git repository" and lists "checkout status" as local state, but never distinguishes committed state from the visible TOML/Markdown files. src/store/git.rs:110-128 resolves head strictly from refs/heads/main and reads blobs from that commit, never from disk. The real producer src/writer/mod.rs:321-340 creates the changed tree and publishes the main ref before src/writer/mod.rs:387-429 updates SQLite and attempts checkout fast-forward; checkout errors only print a warning and the op still returns Committed at line 438. src/writer/worktree.rs:110-121 preserves differing disk bytes and records dirty paths instead of replacing them. Therefore reading or editing the displayed files does not necessarily read or change effective graph state. A brief authority/derived-view statement is a material ownership clarification, rather than requesting every checkout field.

claim: The local journal is described as holding queued operations and recovery state, omitting that it owns the complete live operation lifecycle and terminal outcomes; Git operation records are successful-commit summaries.
evidence: The document labels Git actions/operations "Mutation history" and local SQLite "queued operations ... retries and notices". The real writer src/writer/mod.rs:279-282 and 312-315 finalizes rejection in SQLite and exits before writing a Git operation record; src/writer/mod.rs:259-262 similarly finalizes failures locally. Only the success path calls write_operation_record at line 321, and src/writer/mod.rs:524-533 writes a Committed snapshot with commit=None, rejection=None and superseded_by=None. Journal::cancel at src/journal/mod.rs:394-400 and finish_committed_superseding at lines 324-336 change cancellation/supersession in SQLite; live consumers list_ops and op_detail at src/plan/ops.rs:98-109,134-137 read only the journal. Recovery is not reconstruction of that history from Git: src/writer/mod.rs:624-626 skips Graph-Op trailers with no existing journal row. The existing durable-recovery warning is correct, but naming only queued operations leaves the ownership of rejected/failed/cancelled/superseded outcomes and live status unclear. This is a summary-level ownership omission; it does not assert the document explicitly promises a complete Git audit.

claim: The ownership statement does not qualify where processing-request acknowledgements live when delivery falls back to Notify.
evidence: The document says, 'Actual thread messages and receipts live in herdr-threads.' For processing requests, Cargo.toml:17-22 enables threads-service-ack but explicitly supports falling back to Notify with older services. The real delivery branch in src/transcripts/delivery.rs:195-200 sends notify and returns no message_id. The recipient runs request ack (src/transcripts/delivery.rs:73-74), which the CLI sends to request.ack (src/cli/request.rs:75-76); Transcripts::cmd_ack commits bookkeeping.request_ack without any threads-port write (src/transcripts/mod.rs:596-604). RequestAck sets delivery.dispatched_at and status Dispatched, then writes requests/<id>.toml (src/transcripts/mutations.rs:544-548; src/store/layout.rs:78-79; TOML serialization is src/store/tree.rs:129-145). src/transcripts/mod.rs:682 states the distinction explicitly: 'fallback: ACK lives in graph, not threads (unless the threads-service-ack path is active)'. By contrast, service receipts are polled from herdr-threads and mirrored into request_ack (src/transcripts/liveness.rs:239-260). The document already lists dispatch status at line 42, so this is a qualification gap in the ownership sentence, not evidence that service thread receipts are stored incorrectly. If 'receipts' means only herdr-threads service receipts, the narrow literal claim is accurate; the missing distinction matters for readers trying to find the durable request acknowledgement.
